facts.material: stainless steel pan combined with a glass tray
facts.function: broiling food in an oven (pan/rack holds food, tray catches drippings)
facts.form: composite kitchen article of two mutually adapted components sold together

gri_path: GRI 1: stainless steel component falls in heading 7323 (household kitchen articles of steel); glass tray alone would fall in 7013 (glassware for kitchen use); neither heading covers the whole
GRI 3(a): each heading describes only part of the composite good, so they are equally specific
GRI 3(b): the stainless steel broiler pan gives the essential character (named article, role in broiling, bulk); the glass tray is ancillary
GRI 6: 7323.93 of stainless steel; cooking ware; suffix .35 bakeware (cookware not suitable for stove top use), since a broiler pan is used in the oven

rejected_alternatives.reason: glass kitchenware; the glass tray does not give the essential character of the broiler pan
other cooking ware suitable for stove top use; a broiler pan is oven-only
kitchen ware other than cooking ware; the broiler pan is used to cook food
not a part of an electric oven; it is a free-standing cookware article

missing_facts: Relative value and weight of the stainless steel pan versus the glass tray (confirms essential character)
classification.rationale: The broiler pan combines a stainless steel pan with a glass tray. Headings 7323 and 7013 each cover only one of the materials, so GRI 3(b) applies, and the stainless steel pan, the named article that holds the food for broiling, gives the essential character. Stainless steel cookware used only in the oven is bakeware under 7323.93.00.35. NY K85319 (in force) supports classifying stainless steel cookware accessories in 7323.93, though its goods (barbecue accessories) differ.
